operations.comment: ; Batman Returns (Konami, 1993) - NES, MMC3 (mapper 4), 16 x 8 KiB PRG banks, 256 KiB CHR.
; Commented reconstruction built on the verified phase-1 map (checkpoint pass-004; commentary carried
; forward by physical range from rounds 1-3, previous copies under analysis/round-1/ .. round-3/).
; Bank layout: MMC3 PRG mode 0. Banks 14 ($C000) and 15 ($E000) are fixed. The two
; switchable windows are always loaded as an even/odd pair: even bank at $8000, the
; following odd bank at $A000 (pairs 0/1, 2/3, ... 12/13). Each even bank stores its
; own MMC3 bank number in its first byte ($8000), which BankPushAndMapY reads back
; to remember the current pair before switching.
; Known pair roles (from callers; tentative where noted):
; 0/1   sound driver and music data (SoundUpdate, SoundPlayRequest)
; 2/3   screen/scroll helpers (pair selected by MapBanks2_3 before tile-column updates)
; 4/5   player logic, collisions, vehicle-stage engine, stage-event scripts (bank 5), boss 5-2
; 6/7   enemy/item object handlers (ObjHandlerTable) and stage 4-1 vehicle objects
; 8/9   metasprite and animation-script tables (sprite drawing)
; 10/11 title/menu/intro/story scenes, game-over screen, bosses 1-2/2-3/3-3/4-3/6-2
; 12/13 stage data: palettes, PPU-upload scripts, IRQ split tables, stage tables
; Labels: descriptive names are interpretations from code behaviour. *_Next, *_Loop,
; *_Return, *_Continue, *_Skip are local branch targets inside the preceding routine.
; Names <Owner>_StNN / ObjTNN_Handler / VehTypeNN / IntroStepNN are entries of dispatch
; tables (state or type NN of the owner); their role is described at the owner unless the
; entry has its own comment.
; Data_Bnn_XXXX equates name ROM addresses read by code whose table role is unnamed.
; No phase-1 unknown bytes remain at pass-004. Three lone $60 bytes (bank 10 $8CBA, bank 11 $BBB6,
; bank 15 $FD4A) are 1-byte Data regions by user-directed manual fallback only; their meaning is unknown.
; Object arrays hold 20 one-byte slots; the player occupies slots 16/17
; (written ObjX+PLAYER_SLOT etc.). Many objects use an even/odd slot pair.
; ---- Hardware registers (CPU-visible) ----
; ---- RAM variables (CPU $0000-$07FF); names are interpretations, see notes ----
; general scratch $00-$0F (pointers at $00/$01, $08/$09, $0C/$0D)

; Stage enemy-wave interpreter (pair 12/13): when the scroll position reaches the next
; trigger, load the wave description (enemy group Var14F, count, slot limit, CHR banks
; and sprite palette) and spawn its members (SpawnEnemyGroup). Commands with a high bit are
; dispatched through StageScriptCommand.
; Wave records are 9 bytes: [0] trigger ScrollColumn ($FF ends), [1] fine ScrollX, [2] slot pairs
; (bits 0-1) and enemy group (bits 2-7), [3] StageScriptNext, [4] WaveId, [5] CHR set, [6]
; sprite palette, [7] group data, [8] StageScriptCmd. StageScriptPos is the offset of the next
; record; StageFlags bit7 = a wave is active. Example: the stage $11 (5-1) script at $96A3 (inside the
; bank-12 generic data block) holds the only records that spawn ObjType $32 ($970F, $9718) and $33 ($973C).
; Where each script ends is not established (no terminator confirmed).
; (VramBuffer too full this frame)
; Locate this stage's wave script: WaveScriptSetPtrs[tileset] -> list, StageWaveScriptIndex
; [stage] -> script pointer in Tmp+14. Vertical-scroll stages have no waves here.
; Wait until ScrollColumn reaches the record's column (and, on that column, ScrollX
; reaches the fine position, checked on 8-pixel boundaries). At column 0 a record other than
; $FF triggers at once.
; Trigger: lock the scroll (ScrollFlags bit7), reset the kill count, read the record into the
; wave variables, load its CHR banks and sprite palette and the group data.
; Mark the wave active. Stage $10 sets BossClass 5; in stage $0D waves $0B / $1F set class 3 / 4
; and its other waves class 0; other stages keep the class from the stage header.
; Wave in progress: boss areas (StageFlags bit0) continue in SpawnEnemyGroup's boss path.
; Otherwise, unless all members have appeared (ActiveSlotPairs+1 = EnemiesRemaining), set
; StageFlags bit6; with StageScriptNext bit7 the wave ends when EnemiesRemaining is 0,
; else every free slot pair runs the next script command.
; Wave cleared: clear the active flags, advance StageScriptPos by one record (9 bytes) and
; unlock scrolling unless StageModeFlags bit1 keeps it locked.
; Create the wave's enemy slot pairs: reset state, choose side/position, start the group's
; animation and set hit points.
